criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Slide 1 is genuinely made: 34 recesses in a seven-by-five-less-one carve with two-part contact shadows, and the ten lit cells now sit at index positions 10, 25, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, which I counted off the render and matched cell-for-cell against aggregates['10 rows'].from_claims. Item 27 is correctly dark. Slide 2's internally-lit housing with the open dimension carrying exactly one terminator and running off the right frame edge argues 'equal to or greater than' rather than captioning it. Slide 5's face_sun inversion is the deck's one real turn and its two knockout voids are its value extreme. Against that, four of nine frames are type on a gradient: slide 3 is an empty field with one seam (canvas variance 227.1, lowest in the deck), slide 6's rebuilt lower third is a flat fluted panel (variance 255.8, second lowest), slide 8 leaves the whole lower half of the readout plate void, and slide 9's lower two-thirds is four stacked text blocks with no drawn form. The slide 6 dossier also still says the bottom carries the longest plate and the item type codes when the bottom now carries a milled band, and its focal names the Zack Butler plate the widest lit area while render_report measures it at w=749 against Fedor Mikheev's w=862.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Twenty claims, every one primary_official and fetched 2026-08-22, with five explicit rejections including the hard ones. c20 does an absence correctly, naming the document, counting occurrences at 0 and 30, and stating the method. Slide 7's 'two rows here' and slide 4's 'two filings here' are scoped to the frame with the reasoning written into aggregates. Slide 9's quote correctly stops at 'website' with no closing period per c4. But c19 is the deck's load-bearing claim and it overreaches its own quote: the text says the five columns 'are the whole of what it says about a filing' while the quote is only the header row, with no occurrence count and no stated method, the exact discipline c20 applies and c19 does not. Slide 8's 13 sits in aggregates._undeclarable rather than aggregates[], which is routing around a gate rather than fixing it. And slides 4 and 5 relabel the source's 'Item Type' and 'Filing Description' as TYPE and DESCRIPTION on frames whose whole argument is to read exactly what the row says.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader gets the body, the instrument, the number, the deadline corroborated on slide 8 by the calendar feed in c16, the channel read from the claim URLs and the instruction to refer to Project 58482. Slide 9 is a real act-on-this frame. The deck also correctly names no county because no claim does. What is missing is the stake: across nine frames nothing says what a competitively procured demand-reduction service would do to a reader's bill, their county or their grid. A Texan learns a rule exists and how to comment on it without learning why they would want to.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: Count, definition, requirement, two rows, one row dissected, the rest, the commission's own rows, the clock, the act. The turn is real and it is on slide 5, marked by the deck's only inverted ground. Two drags. Slides 4 through 7 are four consecutive index-row frames and slide 6 is cuttable. And the line 'The rule as published in the Texas Register does not contain the words data center.' appears verbatim on slide 1 and again on slide 2, a repeat inside a single swipe, then a third time in the caption and a fourth in the first comment.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: House rules hold on every published surface I checked. No colons or semicolons in the caption or on any frame, no em or en dashes outside verbatim quotes, ordinals correct throughout, no first person, no sentence opening with And or But, straight apostrophes in copy.json, hashtags present, and writer-chosen commas run about two across 180 words of caption prose. 'A number does the work a name would do' and '34 filings are already in' have snap. What holds it at the rubric's clean, on register, a little flat is that nothing in nine frames is Texan beyond the agency name and ERCOT REGION in slide 9's title block.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: No repeat inside the window: topics.json carries the Grimes County fab, Houston ISD, the Governor's data center audit and Batch Zero, League City ALPR and driverless authorization, and none is Project 58482. The opening move and slide 5's ground inversion are both fresh. Held at 7 for two reasons. The 08-19 entry is also PUCT plus ERCOT plus large load with the Data Center Coalition among its entities, so the beat repeats within three days even though the topic gate is satisfied. And I read topics.json but not artwork.json, so I am scoring technique distinctness on the renders alone and will not claim more than I checked.

hard_fails: An unverified fact presented as verified, on the record this deck's first comment sends readers to. ledger/docket.json item tx-2026-0002 carried last_verified 2026-08-22 and confidence high, and its public_access.how still read 'Individuals have already done so without counsel. The record contains filings from named members of the public alongside utility and data center filings.' Both assertions are in this run's own claims.json rejected list. The summary was corrected and this field was not, and it published three times on docs/item/tx-2026-0002/index.html including in the JSON-LD FAQPage acceptedAnswer. Three sections above it the same page published a dated history line asserting the opposite, which was false about the page it was on. A reader following the deck's own citation from slide 5, which prints 'Nothing here states who a filer is.', landed on the exact claim the deck exists to refute.
one_sentence_fix: Add a gate that reads every published string field of any docket item a run touches (summary, public_access.how, notes_for_editor, history) against that run's claims.json rejected list and fails the build on a match, because this run corrected summary, wrote a history line saying four assertions were fixed, and left the same rejected assertion standing in public_access.how where the site publishes it three times including in JSON-LD.
